title: AgroTrace queue event envelope
description: Common document of every queue event (spec 8.1, 8.2.1). Transport: each backend publishes only to its own durable direct exchange `agrotrace.{backend}` with routing key = `type`; its worker consumes only the durable queue `agrotrace.{backend}.worker` bound to all event types, so an event is handled by exactly one worker of the backend that created it. Express publishes this document as the message body (persistent, content_type application/json, message_id = id); Celery and Laravel Queue pass this document as the single argument of the task/job named by `type` (their own wrapper format is library-defined). Events are published only AFTER the database transaction that caused them commits; a publish failure is retried 3 times (delays 1 s, 2 s, 4 s) and then logged at ERROR level, the API operation still succeeds. Delivery is at-least-once: every handler is idempotent (see each event). A failed handler is retried up to 5 times with delays 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s, then the message goes to the dead-letter queue `agrotrace.{backend}.dead`.

id.description: Event id (UUID v4), also the AMQP message_id; stored as `eventId` in notification payloads for deduplication.

occurredAt.description: Commit time of the causing transaction, ISO 8601 UTC with Z.

requestId.description: X-Request-Id of the API request that caused the event; null for scheduler jobs. An event published by a worker copies the requestId of the event being handled.
